Data Folder
Place any data needed by your analysis in this folder. Please do not store large files here. Then read in any data using the ‘data’ path. For example, read_csv("data/data.csv").

Introduction
[~ 200 words] This is an introduction
Clearly stated background and questions / hypotheses / problems being addressed. Sets up the analysis in an interesting and compelling way. Include figures if you like.


Materials and methods
[~ 200 words]
Exploring Canopy-Cover Dependency of Local Bird Species Canopy cover is a significant factor regarding avian species composition and diversity in an area. For example, a species like the Scarlet Tanager (Piranga olivacea) is usually found only in areas with high canopy cover. Likewise, other species do best with minimal/no canopy cover, such as Eastern Meadowlark (Sturnella magna) and Bobolink (Donicholynx oryzivorus). Survival and reproduction depend on what resources are found in these habitats and how each bird is adapted to their individual niche. My study aims to look at the relationships between canopy cover and species composition in several Western New York counties, with the relationships being able to influence conservation and management actions in the area.
For species occurrence data, I plan to use a package called spocc. This package can generate species occurrence data from several sources, including eBird, iNaturalist, and GBIF records. Below is an example map of Scarlet Tanager (Piranga olivacea) sightings over the counties of Erie, Genessee, Niagara, Orleans, and Wyoming. Due to sightings being generated in the entire bounding box, I aimed to use a roughly rectangular patch of the state where only a small portion of records would likely need to be filtered out.
First we install the packages needed and load them into our library. A quick guide to what each package does (not counting those in tidyverse): Tigris: Allows access to some geographical datasets (counties, townships, etc.) CoveR2: Allows R to interpret and display canopy Terra and Tidyterra: Help with Spatial Analysis of Rasters Spocc: Grants access to ecology databases Dismo and pROC: Allows R to run Species Distribution Model (SDM)

Next, we download a canopy raster by going to the MLCD site. I created a window targeting 2025 canopy data which covers the desired counties. This was downloaded as a TIFF file, then uploaded into the project. Although this code does not work due to the TIFF file not being in the repository (it is very big), it is fairly easily to create one that covers the five counties and put it into the project folder.

canopy <- rast("C:/Users/jorda/Downloads/GEO-511-Final-Project/data/WNY_Canopy_Cover.tiff")

Next, we create a vector layer of just the five counties by filtering the ny_counties dataset provided by tigris. It must be projected, cropped, and masked so that it and the raster are compatible.

ny_counties <- counties(state = "NY", cb = TRUE)

Retrieving data for the year 2025



five_counties <- ny_counties |>
  filter(NAME %in% c("Erie", "Niagara", "Genesee", "Orleans", "Wyoming"))


five_counties_vect <- vect(five_counties)

five_counties_vect <- project(
  five_counties_vect,
  crs(canopy)
)

canopy_ny <- crop(canopy, five_counties_vect)

canopy_ny <- mask(canopy_ny, five_counties_vect)


five_counties_projected <- st_transform(
  five_counties,
  crs(canopy_ny))

Now to plot the new raster to make sure it works

plot(
  canopy_ny,
  main = "Tree Canopy Cover in Western New York"
)








Now make a data frame and plot it as a titled chart

canopy_df <- as.data.frame(
  canopy_ny,
  xy = TRUE,
  na.rm = TRUE
)


ggplot() +
  geom_raster(
    data = canopy_df,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      fill = WNY_Canopy_Cover
    )
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = five_counties_projected,
    fill = NA,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name = "Canopy Cover (%)",
    limits = c(0, 100)
  )+
  labs(
    title = "Canopy Cover in Western New York Counties",
    x = "Easting (meters)",
    y = "Northing (meters)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()








Now to make a bounding box with proper projection for our bird records

five_counties_wgs84 <- st_transform(
  five_counties_projected,
  4326
)

county_bbox <- st_bbox(five_counties_wgs84)
county_bbox <- as.numeric(st_bbox(five_counties_wgs84))

Download the bird data. I requested 3000 Scarlet Tanager “Piranga olivacea” records over a five-year span, though there are only around 1500 available in the database

tanager_data <- occ(
  query = "Piranga olivacea", 
  from = c("gbif", "inat"), 
  geometry = county_bbox, 
  limit = 3000, 
  date = c("2020-01-01", "2025-12-31"), 
  has_coords = TRUE
)


tanager_df <- occ2df(tanager_data)
nrow(tanager_df)

[1] 3055

tanager_clean <- tanager_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude))

tanager_df <- tanager_df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(longitude),
    !is.na(latitude)
  ) %>%
  distinct(longitude, latitude, .keep_all = TRUE)

tanager_sf <- st_as_sf(
  tanager_df,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)

tanager_sf <- st_as_sf(
  tanager_clean,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = 4326
)

tanager_sf <- st_transform(tanager_sf, st_crs(five_counties_projected))

tanager_sf_projected <- st_transform(tanager_sf, crs = st_crs(canopy_ny))


ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = canopy_ny) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "darkgreen",
    name = "Canopy Cover (%)"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = five_counties_wgs84,
    fill = NA,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = tanager_sf_projected,
    color = "red",
    size = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Scarlet Tanager Observations and Canopy Cover",
    subtitle = "Five New York Counties"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

#make GLM SDM model
tanager_points <- terra::project(
  terra::vect(tanager_in_counties),
  terra::crs(canopy_ny)
)

tanager_values <- terra::extract(
  canopy_ny,
  tanager_points
)

presence_data <- data.frame(
  presence = 1,
  canopy = tanager_values[[2]]
)

presence_data <- na.omit(presence_data)

presence_cells <- cellFromXY(
  canopy_ny,
  crds(tanager_points)
)

canopy_background <- canopy_ny

canopy_background[presence_cells] <- NA
set.seed(123)

background_points <- spatSample(
  canopy_background,
  size = 1000,
  method = "random",
  na.rm = TRUE,
  as.points = TRUE
)

background_values <- terra::extract(
  canopy_ny,
  background_points
)

background_data <- data.frame(
  presence = 0,
  canopy = background_values[[2]]
)

background_data <- na.omit(background_data)

sdm_data <- bind_rows(
  presence_data,
  background_data
)
table(sdm_data$presence)


   0    1 
1000 2559 



#This chunk actually puts the parts of the model together
sdm_model <- glm(
  presence ~ canopy,
  data = sdm_data,
  family = binomial()
)


summary(sdm_model)

#Now to actually define suitability values and plot them

suitability <- terra::app(
  canopy_ny,
  fun = function(x) {
    plogis(
      coef(sdm_model)[1] +
        coef(sdm_model)[2] * x
    )
  }
)

global(suitability, "range", na.rm = TRUE)

lyr.1 0.681222 0.8941426

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = suitability) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "darkgreen",
    name = "Relative Suitability"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = five_counties_wgs84,
    fill = NA,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = tanager_in_counties,
    color = "red",
    size = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Scarlet Tanager Species Distribution Model",
    subtitle = "Canopy cover-based habitat suitability",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

#Train the model and run it

set.seed(123)

train_rows <- sample(
  1:nrow(sdm_data),
  size = 0.8 * nrow(sdm_data)
)

train_data <- sdm_data[train_rows, ]
test_data <- sdm_data[-train_rows, ]

test_data$predicted <- predict(
  sdm_model,
  newdata = test_data,
  type = "response"
)

roc_model <- roc(
  test_data$presence,
  test_data$predicted
)
